key_insight: A unified linear compressible theory shows that aerofoil porosity strongly alters unsteady loading and its sensitivity to Mach number, so porous and rigid-load models cannot be combined naively.
engineering_relevance: For flutter, gust response, and flow-control design, porous treatments must be evaluated with compressibility included because the predicted load reduction can be wrong by up to about a factor of two.
method: Couples Possio’s integral operator with a convective permeable boundary condition for finite-chord aerofoils.
Allows chordwise-varying admittance while retaining wake effects and the unsteady Kutta condition.
Uses the incompressible edge/discontinuity exponent form in the local permeability parameter, enabling weighted-Jacobi collocation.
evidence_signal: The model is verified against published incompressible results and an independent compressible formulation, then used for gust, heave, and indicial responses showing 33% to 50% load changes at Mach 0.7 for weak permeability.
watch_item: The porous-to-impermeable load ratio is highly sensitive to compactness and Mach number, so using incompressible porous theory alone can overstate or understate load reduction by large factors.
paper_title: Compressible unsteady aerodynamics of finite-chord porous aerofoils
